study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Oliveira-Saraiva and Ferreira, Frontiers in Psychiatry, 2023
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative model detects abnormal functional connectivity in psychiatric disorders

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: The study used an autoencoder-based normative model implemented with Keras. The architecture consisted of three hidden layers (91-46-13-46-91), with leaky ReLU activation, L2 regularization (1e-5), dropout (0.5), and was trained for 1,000 epochs using Adam optimizer.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Autoencoder was the selected architecture for the generation of the normative model, and it was implemented using the Keras Python library.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Functional connectivity matrices (14x14) were constructed from Pearson's correlation coefficients between BOLD time series of 14 functional brain networks (FBNs). The 91 unique inter-network connectivity values (lower triangular matrix excluding diagonal) were used as features for the normative model.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The Pearson's correlation coefficients between the time series of all FBNs pairs were calculated. In the end, a 14 × 14 functional connectivity matrix was created for each subject, giving information about inter FBNs connectivity.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The autoencoder-based normative model did not include any explanatory variables such as age or sex. The authors explicitly acknowledged this as a limitation.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: we started with a simple autoencoder that received no information about sex/age. The model led to good results, but improvements to it could lead to better results.
